correctness.rationale: After scaling \(w_1=1\), the norm satisfies \(N_a^2=\max\{x^2+ay^2,ax^2+y^2\}\). The Euclidean sandwich \((1+a)\|z\|_2^2/2\le N_a(z)^2\le\|z\|_2^2\) is sharp. For an arbitrary ellipse \(E_A\subset K\subset\lambda E_A\), the two defining quadratic forms imply both diagonal entries of \(A\) are at least one, while the two diagonal boundary points of \(K\) force \(\lambda^2\ge2/(1+a)\), proving the exact affine lower bound. The same sandwich plus the Euclidean parallelogram and Ptolemy identities gives the claimed upper bounds for the two geometric constants, and the displayed axis/diagonal configurations attain them.

originality.rationale: The final equality is implication-level covered by prior results. Saito--Kato--Takahashi give a general exact formula for the von Neumann--Jordan constant of any absolute normalized plane norm comparable with the Euclidean norm; applying it to the \(q=2\) Lorentz norm gives \(C_{\mathrm{NJ}}=2/(1+a)\) by the one-variable ratio at \(t=1/2\). Kato--Maligranda--Takahashi prove \(C_{\mathrm{NJ}}(X)/d(X,Y)^2\le C_{\mathrm{NJ}}(Y)\); with \(Y=\ell_2^2\) this forces \(d_{\mathrm{BM}}^2\ge C_{\mathrm{NJ}}(X)\), while the elementary norm sandwich gives the reverse inequality. Zuo explicitly computes the same Lorentz Ptolemy constant as \(2/(1+a)\). Hence all three equalities follow from published theorems plus routine substitution/comparison.
